# agentic-identity

People, agents, and the access they share: delegation, invites, links, and an audit trail.

Status: 0.6.0 preview. Principals and delegation, sharing (roles, invites, links, audit), six ports (Store, Blobs, Auth, Realtime, Mail, Queue), memory, Firestore (`agentic-identity/firestore`), netlify, file (Node: `createFileStore({ path })`, `createFileBlobs({ dir })` at agentic-identity/file), and Cloudflare D1/R2 adapters, a Store-backed Queue (`createStoreQueue(store)`, runs on D1 or Firestore, call `run()` to deliver), Mail adapters (`createHttpMail` for any https JSON mail API, `createCloudflareMail` for an Email Workers `send_email` binding), contract suites at agentic-identity/testing. HTTP API (agentic-identity/worker) with OIDC sign-in (`oidcProvider(config)`, the `googleProvider(clientId, clientSecret)` preset, `beginLogin`, `finishLogin`, which throws `OidcError`), API keys, personal access tokens, and data export and delete. Typed SDK at agentic-identity/sdk. Shared bearer check at agentic-identity/http: `requirePrincipal(request, auth, { kinds?, scope?, origins? })` returns the principal or a 401/403/503 Response. A write that rides on the session cookie needs an Origin listed in `origins`, or it is a 403; a bearer key needs none. WebSocket sign-in at the same entry: `principalFromWebSocketRequest(request, auth, { protocol, encoding?, kinds?, scope?, origins? })` reads the token from the subprotocol `<protocol>.bearer.<token>` (base64url by default) and returns the principal or a 401/403/503 Response; `acceptWebSocketProtocol(request, response, protocol)` names `<protocol>` on the 101 answer and never the token. CLI `agentic-identity` and MCP server `agentic-identity-mcp`, both on a local JSON file. Account export and erase across apps (agentic-identity/account): one deterministic zip with a manifest, and an erase that audits each app.

## Principal input

Import `PRINCIPAL_KINDS`, `parsePrincipal`, and `subjectOf` from `agentic-identity`. `parsePrincipal(input)` returns `{ kind, id }` or throws `PrincipalParseError` (kind missing or unknown; id not 1 to 128 chars of `A-Za-z0-9._-` starting with a letter, digit, `_` or `-`). `subjectOf(principal)` returns `kind:id`.
